title: Understanding MAE and MSE
text: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Mean Squared Error (MSE) are both metrics used to evaluate the accuracy of a model. MAE calculates the average of the absolute differences between predicted and actual values, while MSE calculates the average of the squared differences.

title: Sensitivity to Outliers
text: Outliers are data points that are significantly different from other observations. Consider how squaring the differences in MSE might affect its sensitivity to these outliers compared to MAE.

title: Comparing MAE and MSE
text: Which error metric, MAE or MSE, is more affected by large errors?

title: Conclusion on Sensitivity
text: Since MSE squares the errors, it gives more weight to larger errors compared to MAE, which only takes the absolute value. Therefore, MSE is more sensitive to outliers than MAE.
